title: Measure what a recorded snapshot carries and what binds two of them
question: does the published record carry any structure that stands for a snapshot of a page, which fields such a structure carries, whether any of those fields binds two records to one page, and whether the record publishes anything at two moments at all?

identity.definition: a field binds two records to one page when the record itself carries it, its value is stable across two records of the same page, its value differs between two different pages, and the tree states that meaning for it. A value that merely repeats (a constant, a mode, a version) fails the third condition; a value that changes per record fails the second; a value with no stated meaning fails the fourth.
identity.statement: No field the record carries is a stable identity of a page. The record's own nine keys are the nine measured above and none is a url, a document key, a tab or a page id; extension/agent-main.js reads no `location`, no `document.URL`, no `href` and no `document.title` at all. The nearest thing is `stability.attachAt`: the one value that repeats across every record of one subscribe, taken once at attach and cleared by the reset path, which the tree never calls an identity. Everything else either increments per record (`cycleId`, `startedAt`), is scoped to one arrival (`routerEvents[].id`, `url`, `matchedPaths`, `boundary.entries[].at`) or is a constant two pages can share (`zoneMode`, `boundary.version`, `stability.version`, both `coreVersion`s, `stability.reachedBy`).

nearest.statement: stable across records of one subscribe, but a clock reading with no stated identity meaning, cleared to null by the reset path, and coincident between two pages: binding on it would be an invention the tree does not support.

twoMoments.statement: No. The record is published at two sites and only two: `closeCycle` (one per change-detection frame, queued as a microtask from the frame a TemplateUpdateStart opens) and `dispatchInitialRecord` (once per install, 500 ms after it). Nothing it publishes is a snapshot of a page at a moment. The frame record carries the frame's own work and the components that frame reported in `checks`; the install record carries the same keys with `events: []` and one check built from the enumerated nodes. The page-shaped parts that repeat across records are cumulative arrival copies (`routerEvents`, `boundary.entries`), which repeat earlier arrivals rather than describe the page now, and the one router state snapshot the code reads is consumed inside a single event entry and reduced to its route-config path strings, never published as a snapshot.

evidence.lineText: // The snapshot carries the same list a frame carries, empty.
// The router list and the boundary record are not frame-scoped: they carry the arrivals.
// The primary chain's own config paths, in order, and nothing else: no snapshot object, no URL tree

twoMoments.decides: SC1 as the roadmap states it — two recorded snapshots of the same page compared field by field — has no input in this record: the record publishes no page snapshot at all, at one moment or at two. What it publishes at many moments is a frame record whose page-shaped keys are partial (the frame's components), cumulative (the arrival lists) or install-time (the boundary and stability answers). SC2 is therefore the normal case rather than an edge: no field of the record binds two records to one page, so a pair of records cannot be established as the same page from the record's own fields.

verdict: Measured, and the measurement refuses the roadmap's premise: this record publishes no page snapshot at any moment, so it publishes none at two. The structures it carries that could be mistaken for one — the frame's `checks`, the router entry that reduces a router state snapshot to `matchedPaths`, and the `boundary`/`stability` sections — are a frame's own components, one event's fields and cumulative arrival lists. No field of the record binds two of its records to one page: the only value that repeats across records of one page session is `stability.attachAt`, a clock reading the tree never calls an identity and the reset path clears. SC1 therefore has no input in this record and SC2 is the normal case rather than an edge.

consequences: SC2 is the normal case: no field of the record binds two of its records to one page, so a pair that a surface cannot bind is every pair.

SC1 as written — two recorded page snapshots compared field by field — has no input in this record. The record publishes records at many moments and page snapshots at none; a comparison over a "page snapshot" would be a comparison over a shape the record does not publish.

What repeats across records is not a snapshot: `routerEvents` and `boundary.entries` are cumulative arrival copies (the same earlier arrivals reappear in every later record), and `checks` is the frame's own components.

The nearest per-page value is `stability.attachAt`: stable across every record of one subscribe, cleared to null by the reset path, and never stated to identify a page. Treating it as a page identity would be an invention, not a measurement.

A refusal can name what is missing, because the record states its absences: no url on the record (only per-event `url`/`urlAfterRedirects`, null where the event carried none), no tab or page key (the envelope's `tabId` is added by the background), no install identifier (only the incrementing `cycleId` and the clearable `attachAt`), and only the Angular version, which two pages of one build share.
